item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00035","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C14","C12","C05"],"selected_candidate_label":"C14","confidence":0.74,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C14 plausibly supplied a material structural template: both memoranda reject a private lump-sum relief bill after reviewing an existing administrative compensation process, then emphasize that the claimant can still pursue relief through that process and expressly endorse a procedural measure or reconsideration designed to produce a result fair to both the claimant and the Government. C12 is substantively close because it concerns a serviceman's death, established survivor benefits, and a benefit the decedent declined, but it lacks the child's alternative-remedy conclusion. C05 also ends by preferring an established adjudicative remedy, though its contract and judicial-remedy setting is less closely aligned.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the beneficiary can now have her claim settled administratively... Reconsideration of the beneficiary's claim under such legislation would result in an award which, I am confident, will be equitable from the standpoint of both the beneficiary and the government.","parent_excerpt":"the claimant should be afforded the opportunity to advance any additional evidence he may have in support of his claim... the claim will be processed under accepted procedures, fair to both the individual and the Government.","explanation":"Both reject the proposed direct award but conclude by channeling the claimant into an established administrative process expressly characterized as fair to claimant and Government."},{"child_excerpt":"I can perceive no justification for the payment which the bill would make... He was, at all times, entitled to such care at facilities operated by the Navy Department.","parent_excerpt":"I find no justification for this proposed award... the claimant was entitled to periodic disability compensation under laws administered by the Bureau of Employees' Compensation","explanation":"The argumentative sequence is parallel: no justification for the special award because an established benefit system governed the underlying injury or care."},{"child_excerpt":"I should like to express my belief that the Board should take into account, in its reconsideration of the case, the possibility that... medical treatment... might very well have led to his retention on active duty","parent_excerpt":"I believe that the claimant should be afforded the opportunity to advance any additional evidence he may have in support of his claim.","explanation":"Each recommends renewed administrative consideration of evidence after withholding approval of the private bill."}]}
